ingest.note: Consumes text chunks; no audio input.

egress.note: Output format is chosen via output_format = codec_sampleRate_bitrate. Options include mp3_22050_32, mp3_44100_128, pcm_16000, pcm_44100, and ulaw_8000_8 (μ-law 8 kHz, native for Twilio/telephony).

potholes.note: ElevenLabs can emit ulaw_8000_8 directly. For a Twilio/Exotel μ-law leg, request this format to SKIP the resample + μ-law encode stage entirely. Falls back to PCM/MP3 + your own encode if unavailable.
If you select an MP3 format, streaming MP3 needs a stateful decoder (not per-chunk) before resampling. Prefer pcm_16000 or ulaw_8000_8 to avoid decoding entirely.

First-byte latency dominates perceived responsiveness. Use Flash v2.5 for realtime TTS, keep a persistent WebSocket, stream LLM text promptly, and consider auto_mode plus deployment-region proximity. Avoid legacy latency-tuning query parameters.
Flash v2.5 disables text normalization by default to preserve latency, so normalize phone numbers, dates, and currencies before TTS (or use the Enterprise normalization option).

Keep one WebSocket for streaming LLM text. auto_mode avoids manual chunk schedules; without it, insufficient text stalls generation. Voice choice, speaker boost, style, and higher-fidelity formats can add latency.

cost_estimates.notes: Architecture-planning allowance only; verify current Flash v2.5 account pricing before a production cost SLO

latency_evidence.methodology: Callsmith architecture-budget placeholder; benchmark in the deployment region before setting an SLO.

interruption.description: On interruption, stop consuming the streaming TTS WebSocket. Discard any buffered audio chunks. Cancel the text input stream.
interruption.code_hint: Close the ElevenLabs streaming WebSocket and clear your TTS output buffer. Pipecat handles this via InterruptionFrame; LiveKit via session cancellation.

deployment.self_host_notes: Managed streaming API; no model self-host path is declared in this pack.
